description: Top-level blueprint field selecting target platform. String or list. Allowed values: `default` (alias for linux), `linux`, `windows`. List form (`[default, windows]`) runs identical commands on each platform, producing one snapshot per platform. For platform-specific commands use multi-block YAML.
Top-level blueprint section. Holds steps that run ONCE during builds; results persist in the snapshot. Use for language runtimes, system packages, global CLI tools.
Top-level blueprint section. Runs during builds AND surfaced (not auto-executed) to the agent at session start. Should be fast and incremental; use `npm install`, not `npm ci`.
Top-level blueprint section. Reference info loaded into Devin's context at session start (NOT executed). Lightweight, focused on executable command refs (lint/test/build).
Human-readable label for a blueprint step. Surfaced in build logs.
Shell-script body for a blueprint step. Must be non-interactive — interactive commands hang and time out. Subject to a 1-hour per-step timeout.

GitHub Action reference, e.g., `github.com/actions/setup-node@v4`. Devin downloads and runs the action during build, the same way GitHub CI runners execute action steps. Supported for setup-python, setup-node, setup-go, etc.
Inputs passed to a referenced GitHub Action. E.g., `with: { node-version: '20' }` for `actions/setup-node@v4`.
Identifier for a knowledge entry — e.g., `lint`, `test`, `build`. Used by Devin to look up the canonical command for a category.
Body of a knowledge entry — typically a single executable command (e.g., `npm run lint`). NOT executed by the runtime; loaded into Devin's context as reference info.

Multi-document YAML separator. Lets a single blueprint editor file contain multiple blocks — used for multi-platform blueprints (one block per `runs-on`) and for organizing complex blueprints into logical sections.

Reference syntax for secrets stored in Devin's Secrets dashboard. Available in blueprint shell commands and live session shells. Place credential-writing steps in `maintenance` (not `initialize`) so credentials are refreshed on each periodic build.

Per-step timeout during a build. Steps exceeding this are killed and the build fails. Common cause of hits: compiling large native dependencies from source — use pre-built binaries instead. Also triggered by commands waiting for interactive input.

Timeout for a single command during the classic-config repo-setup wizard. Cognition explicitly recommends against giving Devin commands that take longer than 5 minutes — performance degrades significantly.
Approximate cadence at which builds run automatically to refresh dependencies. Skipped while a snapshot is pinned.
Maximum age of a build that's still pinnable. Builds older than 7 days cannot be pinned. Status must also be Success or Partial.
Typical end-to-end build time for an org's blueprint(s). Used for capacity planning when waiting on a fresh snapshot.
Default home directory for the DevBox user on Linux. Used in path-based blueprint commands that need an absolute reference.
Default home directory on Windows DevBox (Git-Bash-style path).
Per-repo working-tree path. On Linux: /home/ubuntu/repos/<repo-name>. On Windows: /c/Users/Administrator/repos/<repo-name>. Each configured repo lives in its own subdirectory.
Directory where uploaded files are written. Linux: /home/ubuntu/.files/. Windows: /c/Users/Administrator/.files/. Files dragged-and-dropped into the embedded VS Code instance land here.
Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint exposed by DevBox's Chrome browser. Playwright connects here for browser-based authentication automation and systematic data entry.
User shell init file inside DevBox. Direnv hook is pre-configured. Common edits: PATH manipulation, per-repo `nvm use` cd-hooks. Edit via `devin ~/.bashrc`.
Per-repo environment-variable file consumed by direnv. Created at the repo root; loaded after running `direnv allow` once.
Location to which the user uploads `config.ovpn`. Drag-and-drop into the VS Code instance; choose any path in DevBox (typically /etc/openvpn/ or ~/).
Path to the systemd unit file that auto-starts OpenVPN at session boot. Created by the user during VPN setup; references the config.ovpn from the previous step.
Devin egress IP — must be allowlisted on customer firewalls / SCM allowlists / internal services. Documented in Admin > Common Issues > IP Whitelisting.
Devin egress IP (allowlist target).
Devin egress IP (allowlist target).
Devin egress IP (allowlist target).
Devin egress IP (allowlist target).
Devin egress IP (allowlist target).
Devin egress IP (allowlist target).
Repo state: has a blueprint with initialize/maintenance/knowledge — fully set up in the snapshot.
Repo state: cloned into the snapshot but no custom blueprint. Devin can read the code but has no setup commands for it.
Repo state: connected to the org but not added to the environment. Not cloned. Visible in repo selector but not yet usable.
Build status: all steps completed; snapshot is ready to use.
Build status: some repo-level steps failed; snapshot is usable. Repos that succeeded work normally; repos that failed need their blueprints fixed.
Build status: critical failure (org or enterprise tier setup failed). Snapshot is NOT usable.
Build status: superseded by a newer build or manually cancelled.
Cognition's recommended per-session ACU ceiling. Beyond ~10 ACU per session, agent performance noticeably degrades. Soft cap (the product nudges, doesn't enforce).
Threshold above which usage-based billing triggers an immediate bill (rather than waiting for end-of-cycle). Whichever comes first: hitting $2,000 in additional usage OR end of billing cycle.
UI location of the Large Performant (Beta) VM-tier toggle. Default for new teams; existing teams must opt in (requires resetting machine setup; experimental auto-migration via support@cognition.ai).
Default shell on Windows DevBox. Same bash semantics as Linux DevBox — most blueprint commands work cross-platform without modification.
Git Bash path style on Windows DevBox (e.g., /c/Users/Administrator instead of C:\Users\Administrator). Required when Windows-specific paths appear in blueprint commands.
Available package managers on Windows DevBox: Chocolatey (choco), winget, or direct download scripts. apt-get is NOT available.
Default package manager on Linux DevBox.

AGENTS.md section listing setup commands the agent should run. Devin reads this before starting work. Example entries: 'Install dependencies: npm install', 'Start development server: npm run dev', 'Run tests: npm test', 'Build for production: npm run build'.
AGENTS.md section listing code-style requirements (e.g., 'Use TypeScript strict mode', 'Prefer functional components in React', 'Use ESLint and Prettier configurations').
AGENTS.md section listing testing requirements (frameworks, coverage targets, when to run).
AGENTS.md section enumerating top-level directories (e.g., '/src - Main application code', '/tests - Test files', '/docs - Documentation', '/public - Static assets').
AGENTS.md section describing branching/PR/commit conventions.
All data transmission encrypted in transit. Production systems also routinely monitored via logging, error handling, live-metrics dashboards.
Data encrypted at rest in Cognition's AWS production environment.

Whether the customer's data may be used for Cognition model training. Default false (opt-out by default). Toggle on the Data Controls settings page. Enterprise customers' data is NEVER used for training regardless of toggle.
All Cognition employees and contractors required to use multi-factor authentication on all main work applications.
Cognition's production cloud environment is hosted in AWS.
Address for security vulnerability reports. Documented in Admin > Security.
Customer-support contact address. Used for VM-tier auto-migration requests, integration issues, and other operational asks.
